instances.guard: An automatic writer never writes back a person's columns it read earlier. In Detector.save: open BEGIN IMMEDIATE just before the DELETE, re-read status, notes, recovered_cents, recovered_date, appealed_at, status_changed_at and the newest manual event id per finding, and for every finding a person changed since the read keep the current values (and mark its state for the next run) before writing; count them in the run manifest. Better: stop DELETE plus INSERT and UPDATE the run's own columns with WHERE status_version = <read>. Every rule-driven UPDATE (_hide_matching, unhide, rematch) adds AND status = <expected> and counts rows changed. Close every cursor before the write so a person's save never kills the run.

class_guard: Every write is a compare-and-set against what its author saw, enforced where and when it is applied, and every refusal or loss is kept and shown. Spec for a builder: (1) One write path. remitwatch/writes.py (or actions.py) exposes apply_person_write(conn, kind, target, expected, change, actor, entry_id) and every state-changing route on both hosts, the Vercel fold, import-cloud and the CLI go through it. Each kind names its version: item status (status plus a status_version integer column bumped by every status write, a person's or the run's); bulk (that per item); payer fax number (the number); hide rule (rule key, at, and the count it hides now); write-off policy (decision and the count now); held report (status, decision); alert acknowledgement (severity and figures); fax settle (status sending, provider_id null); fax tie (tied, decision); note match (status, matched_at); spot answer (answer). A write whose expected version differs changes nothing: server 409 {code: changed, now, by, at}; Vercel checks the serving copy at request time and the journal entry carries expected; the fold re-checks on the raw store and a mismatch writes a 'not_applied' event on the item and a count in status.json, and the page shows a person their own refused changes. (2) Automatic writers obey the same rule. Detector.save never writes back a person's columns it read earlier: re-read them under BEGIN IMMEDIATE before writing and keep any changed since (better: UPDATE its own columns WHERE status_version = read); every rule UPDATE (hide pass, unhide, rematch, mark-sent-after-send) adds AND <version> = expected; a person's save never makes a run fail. (3) The journal: each entry has an id (dedup by id), carries expected, and 'last change by time wins' on every copy (apply_status keeps the status when the entry is older than the item's newest manual change); serverless reservations and status checks force a journal read first; an entry that cannot land is moved to the item's heir or, after 7 days, listed as a dropped change, never deleted silently. (4) In-flight state is visible: sends and preparations hold a per-item lock row (Vercel: a marker file written with mode add) that every other write on the item checks (409 in_flight). (5) Pages: every write sends the version it was drawn from and the id it was rendered for; every action button is disabled from the first activation until its answer, ignores key auto-repeat and activations within ~800 ms of the panel drawing a new item; code after an await touches the panel only if it still shows the same item; sweeping writes (hide, policy, bulk, 'send all') show the count, dollars and destination and send them back, and owner-class writes need the owner's password where one is set. (6) A unit test per kind (stale version refused, both hosts) and the property test below are release gate 8; test_l4_stale_writes.py's 15 cases must pass on push 2.
property_test: Generated multi-actor test, both hosts (release gate 8). Build an invented store (tests/test_features builders, a few hundred items over three payers, faxes, held reports, alerts, notes, hide rules and policy rows). Generate a random schedule of 50-500 steps interleaving: people (2-4 actors, each with tabs whose screen is a snapshot of object versions taken at a random earlier step) doing single status, bulk status, hide add or remove, policy accept or pursue, fax number save or confirm, held report apply or discard, fax settle, fax tie, alert ack, note match, spot answer, double submits and key repeats; and the system doing detection runs (later payment closes items, a signal change gives an item a new id, a takeback reopens one), fax runs (settle sent or failed), alert runs (re-raise worse), and on Vercel cron folds at random points, two ServingCopy instances reading the journal in random arrival orders, a replay of the whole journal twice, and entry expiry. On the server, person writes are injected inside the run's save through the connection's trace callback (after the read and at the DELETE). Invariants after every schedule: I1 no stale landing: every person write that changed an object found it at the version on its author's screen; I2 no silent loss: every person write is applied (current, or superseded by a later write whose author saw it), refused with a 409 to its author, recorded as not_applied, still pending, or listed as dropped; no automatic writer reverts one (status after any run equals the last applied person status unless a later person write changed it); I3 one decision, one line: duplicates (double submit, key repeat, replay twice, any order) leave one history line and the same final state; I4 convergence: the server store and the Vercel store fed the same writes end with identical statuses, numbers, rules, decisions and histories (ignoring run ids), and two serving copies end identical whatever the arrival order; I5 authority: no hide, policy decision or bulk change lands without the owner's password where set and a confirmed count equal to the count at application time; no fax goes to a number its sender did not see; I6 pages (Playwright on invented stores, both hosts): random double and triple clicks, key auto-repeat on s and l, slow and out-of-order answers and panel switches during awaits; the server's write log holds only (finding_id, seen_status) pairs that were on screen for at least the dwell time before the activation. Seeds that fail are saved as named regression tests.
